input.context: FEAT-183 is a large reflective-prompt-evolution feature (GEPA). The spec covers: eval pipeline, rubric scoring, Pareto ranking, soak monitor, promotion gate, /crew:gepa-eval and /crew:gepa-optimize CLI commands, evals/ test harness, and 8 cross-agent eval datasets. The spec is 900 lines. Decompose it into implementable slices with dependency ordering, effort estimates, and CHECKPOINT gates that are failure modes — if a CHECKPOINT fails, downstream slices are blocked.
constraints: Each slice must be implementable by one builder in 1–3 days
Slices that touch gepa-core (library) must be separate from slices that touch dev-team (consumer)
CHECKPOINT gates must be testable without live LLM calls (dry-run or synthetic data)
Autonomous-safe=false for slices touching agent prompts or rubric authorship

expected_output.summary: 10-slice wave plan: S1 EvalCase schema, S2 TrialStore + fileStore, S3 rubricScorer, S4 Pareto rank, S5 soak monitor, S6 promotion gate, S7 architect eval dataset, S8 /crew:gepa-eval CLI, S9 /crew:gepa-optimize CLI, S10 evals/ harness. Two CHECKPOINTs: after S4 (Pareto rank regression detectable) and after S7 (soak harness detects crafted regression).
expected_output.non_goals_explicit: Does not include a UI dashboard; does not productionise LLM judge infrastructure; FEAT-185/186 (cost + provider) are separate FEATs
failure_modes_named: CHECKPOINT-1 fails: Pareto rank does not deterministically rank the same candidates across re-runs (non-deterministic scorer)
CHECKPOINT-2 fails: soak harness cannot detect crafted regression in rolling 1-day window — promotion mechanism is broken, block S8/S9
slice ordering error: gepa-core slices must land + publish before dev-team consumer slices run

dependencies_graphed.gepa_core_library: slices S1-S6 land in gepa-core repo; each published as a MINOR semver bump
dependencies_graphed.dev_team_consumer: slices S7-S10 land in dev-team; consume gepa-core via npm overrides pinning branch SHA until publish
dependencies_graphed.checkpoint_gate: CHECKPOINT-1 after S4 uses bun test with synthetic Trials; CHECKPOINT-2 after S7 uses crafted regression test

interfaces_typed.EvalCase: { id, input, expected_output?, rubric?, held_out, notes? }
interfaces_typed.Trial: { id, agent, phase, candidate_prompt_hash, score: ScoreResult, source: 'eval'|'captured'|'soak', pareto_rank, created_at }
interfaces_typed.PromotionPolicy: { minPassDelta, minCaseScoreFloor, soakDays, minSoakTrials, maxSoakDays, soakEpsilon, allowCostRegression, allowLatencyRegression }

expected_output.test_strategy_present: Each slice has unit tests; CHECKPOINTs are automated integration tests that can run on synthetic data without live LLM calls; CHECKPOINT-2 is the hardest gate (requires rolling-window soak harness)
expected_output.tradeoffs_articulated: 10 slices vs 5 slices: 10 allows parallelism on gepa-core vs dev-team tracks; 5 slices would couple library and consumer changes in single PRs making rollback harder. 10 chosen for independent reviewability and rollback granularity.
